title: Masks
author: William Saville
content:
Deep breaths,
Tears as I take,
Eyes cast down,
So much at stake.
Heart pounding,
Ribs aching,
If I speak up,
I'm only faking.
Attention seeker,
Nothing but a whore,
Cast down and aside,
How I long for more.
Unloved and unwanted,
By family and former lovers,
Ache for the gentle touch,
Of truly loving mothers.
Grew up weak,
Grew up strong,
Resilient and fragile,
Right and wrong.
Trauma twisted me,
Made me hard yet soft,
Made me desperate for love,
Yet I hold my heart aloft.
Build so many walls,
Let them down too quick,
Give trust to the wrong people,
Then the abandonment makes me sick.
My body is covered in scars,
To match my tortured soul,
If causing me pain is this universe's plan,
It has long since reached its goal.
Smile brightly as a star in the sky,
Laugher permeates the air,
I tell jokes and banter,
Do it all with flare.
Behind closed doors,
That mask falls hard and fast,
The lies I tell others,
The image that I cast.
When I say "I'm fine,"
Or "nothing is wrong with me,"
The lies slide off my tongue,
Leaving my soul bloody.
